labels.text: Section 2010(c)(3): the basic exclusion amount for estates of decedents dying, and gifts made, on the stated date. Only the two dates on which the statute itself fixes an EXACT, not-yet-inflation-adjusted dollar figure are pinned here (the first day of the $5,000,000 base under section 2010(c)(3)(A)-(B) as originally enacted, and the first day of the $15,000,000 base Pub. L. 119-21 section 70106 substitutes effective for estates of decedents dying and gifts made after December 31, 2025). An indexed year is pinned only where the Revenue Procedure publishing it is pinned in `us.irc.inflation_adjustments` (2025: Rev. Proc. 2024-40). Years 2012-2024 remain gaps between the anchored rows, so evaluation returns MISSING_PARAMETER_VALUE rather than a fabricated indexed figure. See TECH-GAPS.md G81.

section 2010(c)(3)(A): 'the basic exclusion amount is $5,000,000', for a decedent dying in calendar year 2011 itself (section 2010(c)(3)(B) only increases this amount for a decedent dying in a calendar year AFTER 2011, so 2011 is the one year with no inflation adjustment yet applied)

Rev. Proc. 2024-40 section 2.41: 'For an estate of any decedent dying in calendar year 2025, the basic exclusion amount is $13,990,000' — the section 2010(c)(3)(B) cost-of-living adjustment published by the Secretary; section 3.02 applies it to events in calendar year 2025, and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 section 3 leaves it unmodified

Pub. L. 119-21 section 70106(a)(1): section 2010(c)(3)(A) as amended, '$15,000,000', for a decedent dying in calendar year 2026 itself (section 70106(a)(2) moves the no-adjustment-yet base year for the inflation formula from 2011 to 2026, so 2026 is again the one year with no adjustment yet applied); effective for estates of decedents dying and gifts made after December 31, 2025
